Subject: Private deployment - residency, backups and wipe evidence

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're close to finalizing the Private (VPC) deployment for Medica Health but have three compliance gating questions from our InfoSec team:

1) Residency guarantees: can you guarantee all customer-controlled storage (blobs, backups, snapshots) will remain in eu-west-1 (Ireland) with no cross-region replication?
2) Backups & retention: what is your default backup cadence and retention for private tenants, and can we opt-out of automatic snapshots?
3) Deletion evidence: when we request a tenant handback and erase, what evidence can you provide (logs, snapshot manifests, key destruction attestations) and how long does that take?

Can you send a concise statement we can pass to our auditors, and any attachments/examples of the wipe evidence you provide? We need to sign the SOW next week.

Best,
Patrick O'Neill
Head of Platform Security, Medica Health
patrick.oneill@medica.com

Subject: Re: Private deployment - residency, backups and wipe evidence

Hi Patrick — thanks for the clear list. Summary answers below; attaching our tenant erase process and SOC2 supplement for auditors.

1) Residency guarantees:
- For Private/VPC deployments you select the cloud region (we support a list of certified regions; for you that will be eu-west-1).
- Storage (persistent volumes, object stores containing tenant blobs and snapshots) is mounted in your dedicated tenant storage within that region. By default there is no cross-region replication for private tenants unless explicitly enabled in the deployment contract.
- We can include a contractual geo-binding clause in the SOW to restrict all customer data to eu-west-1.

2) Backups & retention:
- Default snapshot cadence: incremental snapshots every 6 hours; full daily snapshot. Default retention window: 30 days.
- For Private customers we offer an opt-out or custom retention policy (e.g., disable automated snapshots, or shorten retention to 7 days).
- Snapshots are stored in the same region and subject to the geo-binding clause when requested.

3) Deletion / handback evidence:
- Workflow: (a) customer requests handback, (b) we schedule erase window, (c) ops executes tenant wipe (application level purge + object delete + snapshot expiration + overwrite of ephemeral storage), (d) KMS key rotation and destruction of tenant-specific key material where keys are customer-managed or rotated per contract.
- Evidence package we provide (examples attached):
  * Erase execution log (timestamped ops runbook output)
  * Storage object manifest before/after (hashes and counts)
  * Snapshot deletion receipts and retention-policy change log
  * KMS key rotation record (or KMS key deletion confirmation if Redwood-managed and permitted)
  * Final attestation: signed statement from Redwood Operations describing actions taken and timestamp window.
- Typical turnaround: 3–7 business days, dependent on snapshot retention windows and contractual approvals. For urgent handbacks we can accelerate to 48–72 hours if you accept a short maintenance window and agree to a one-time acceleration fee.

Attachments: Tenant_Erase_Process_v2.pdf (detailed runbook) and SOC2-Supplement.pdf (controls mapping).

Next steps: Monica from Customer Success will follow up with a tailored retention policy and ops timeline; Marissa will confirm the exact wording for the geo-binding clause for the SOW. Happy to hop on a short call if that helps.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference.com

[Attachment: Tenant_Erase_Process_v2.pdf (PDF)]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment - residency, backups and wipe evidence

Hi Patrick — looping in operational detail you can share with auditors. Quick clarifications: 

- Snapshots & backups: by default snapshots are incremental (references only changed blocks) and are immutable for the configured retention window. When you request a wipe we expire the snapshot objects and issue deletion receipts. If you choose to disable automatic snapshots, we still recommend a short retention snapshot during cutover so rollback remains possible until the erase is confirmed.

- Physical deletion vs. logical delete: object stores in cloud providers perform eventual object reclaim; our process issues deletes and then forces object re-write (zero-fill overwrite) on ephemeral/ephemeral-ish volumes where possible, and requests provider-backed object purge for immutable storage. We capture provider deletion receipts when available.

- KMS options: recommended for highest assurance is customer-managed keys (CMK) in your own tenant KMS; Redwood will never retain plaintext keys. If CMK is used, a key rotation + disable event provides strong cryptographic proof of unavailability. If Redwood manages keys, we provide rotation and deletion logs and can include an HSM-backed attestation where required.

- Audit artifacts: we provide a single ZIP containing logs, manifests, receipts and the signed attestation. We can also deliver that ZIP to a secure share (your S3 or GF drive) or via a notarized third party if needed for legal hold evidence.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: confirm retention policy & opt-outs on SOW
- +2 business days: ops ticket RWI-2148 created and erase window proposed
- +3–7 business days post-approval: execute and deliver evidence ZIP

If you confirm 'disable auto-snapshots' in SOW, please also confirm whether you want CMK or Redwood-managed keys.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.inference.com

1) Please add the geo-binding clause to the SOW limiting all data to eu-west-1 (no cross-region replication) and call out that backup artifacts are also region-bound.
2) We will take CMK (customer-managed keys) in our KMS; please confirm integration steps so we can provision an IAM role and key policy.

Also, please include the erase evidence ZIP in a secure transfer to our S3 bucket (we'll provide bucket details after SOW). We may ask for a notarized attestation depending on audit scope; can Redwood accommodate a third-party witness?

If you can draft the SOW language and a short 1–page attestation template, we can get this signed by Friday.
